scientific_question: Does replacing the failed fixed selected-rank96 bottleneck with the complete detector-space K3 dual certificate expose a cross-trajectory target that simple observation-only controls can approximate before any nonlinear model is trained?

target.definition: The deterministic detector-space certificate z3 satisfying x_K3=A^T z3 for the frozen zero-start CGLS trajectory.
target.normalization: divide both observation and z3 by the per-frame observation RMS

shared_downstream.path: proposal -> exact A^T lift -> observable alpha in [0,2] -> unchanged CGLS K1

arms.definition: ordinary least-squares gain for each frozen detector view-component, fit on the four outer-train trajectories
one diagonal gain per complete detector DCT atom
arms.selection: inner leave-one-trajectory-out mean normalized-certificate relative-L2; ties choose the smaller ridge

arms.definition: copy the normalized z3 target of the maximum-cosine-similarity outer-train observation
use the held-out z3 itself; non-deployable target-attainability control

decision_order: The full K3 certificate oracle must reproduce K4 and pass compatibility on all five fit trajectories, otherwise stop the full-view target route.
Report every simple arm on every held-out trajectory; no trajectory may be hidden by pooled averages.
A simple arm is a cross-trajectory candidate only if it passes the unchanged compatibility gate on all five held-out trajectories.
Failure of simple arms does not authorize a larger model by itself; it only separates representation attainability from simple observation-to-target predictability.
